reason: The pleural membranes seem like the link between the lungs and chest, though I don't yet know exactly how they attach.
expectation: The membranes will join or surround the lungs as a first step toward connecting them to the chest.

effect: The lungs now have two pleural membranes with fluid between them; the chest still needs connecting.
reaction: The two separate layers make the connection more interesting than a simple covering.
reason: The outer pleural membrane seems like the next connection to the rib cage.
expectation: The covered lungs will connect to the chest through the pleural layers.

effect: The lungs and rib cage are connected, and the breathing-muscle slot remains empty.
reaction: The diaphragm attachment makes the remaining step clear.
reason: The diaphragm is a breathing muscle and fits the named empty slot.
expectation: The diaphragm will be fitted beneath the rib cage, connecting the breathing muscles to the apparatus.

effect: The diaphragm completes the apparatus and shows how chest expansion draws air in and lung recoil helps air leave.
reaction: Seeing how the diaphragm moves the lungs through the pleural interface was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the diaphragm was most worthwhile because the result connected the parts to the movement of air, not just their locations.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the pleural membranes was less informative on its own: it showed the layers but did not yet explain how they help move the lungs.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the diaphragm pulls the lungs outward through the pleural interface rather than attaching directly to them.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary, though I initially followed the idea that the membranes linked lungs and chest without knowing exactly how.

continue.text: I would continue to see how another body system connects to breathing, although this chapter's choices were fairly straightforward.
